full_judgment: 30. Granting or refusing injunction is a matter of discretion. Injunction granted by the Court of first instance calls for interference by the appellate Court if the conclusion can be reached that the exercise of discretion in favour of the plaintiff is contrary to settled principles of law for the grant of temporary injunction or that the same is arbitrary and perverse. To put it differently, the appellate Court will not interfere with the exercise of discretion of the Court of first instance and substitute its own discretion except where the discretion has been shown to have been exercised arbitrarily or capriciously or perversely. An appeal against exercise of discretion is said to be an appeal on principle. The law as to the reversal by a Court of appeal of an order made by a Court below in the exercise of its discretion is well established.
